input.question: Why are we able to cross our eyes and unable to do the opposite?
input.ground_truth: Some people can do just that. Otherwise, it just fucks with your brain trying to put two images from both eyes at different angles together. Crossing out eyes focuses on something in front of us. Making the eyes look in their own direction doesn't do us any good for survival, so the skill never really evolved

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Why are we able to cross our eyes and unable to do the opposite?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine your eyes are like two balloons on strings. You can pull the strings together and make the balloons (your eyes) meet in the middle—that’s crossing your eyes!

But you can’t pull the strings in the other direction to make your eyes go behind your head. That’s because your eyes are stuck in your head and can only move so much. They can look left, right, up, and down, but not all the way around or behind your head. So, you can cross your eyes, but you can’t make them go the other way like that.
